summary.text: A 72-year-old man with severe GOLD IV COPD, mMRC grade 3 dyspnea and long-term oxygen had limited indoor activity, although he drove to weekly outpatient visits. Pre-admission FEV1 was 0.60 L (28.8% predicted), FEV1/FVC 33.7%, VC 1.79 L (57.4% predicted) and FVC 1.78 L (57.1% predicted). He was admitted for his second lifetime AECOPD after dyspnea at rest, with barrel chest, diminished breath sounds, Hoover sign and accessory-muscle hypertrophy, hyperinflated lungs, and reported compensated respiratory acidosis under 2 L/min nasal oxygen (pH 7.31/PaCO2 59.6/PaO2 59/HCO3 29.5). He was underweight (BMI 15.6/GNRI 86.1), with no significant inflammatory, anemia or renal dysfunction by narrative; all admission table values are retained.

Inpatient care included corticosteroids, bronchodilators, prophylactic antibiotics, ABG-titrated oxygen, twice-daily pulmonary rehab 5–6 days/week, nutrition/pharmaceutical support and counseling. After discharge he received weekly outpatient conditioning, resistance and 20-minute ergometer work at 40% predicted maximum workload targeting Borg 4–5. Dyspnea/exercise intolerance and participation worsened; activity at 2–3 METs produced Borg >5, and wheezing/dyspnea with recurrent AECOPD led to week-eight readmission. Phase 1 6MWD fell 290→220 m, CAT rose 16→19, and SGRQ symptoms 88→95; CSQ-8 was 21 with lower satisfaction on treatment/time-support items.

After inpatient stabilization, an eight-week combined outpatient/video rehabilitation program mirrored the outpatient exercises by videoconference and visually confirmed diet/bronchodilator use. Home activity and unsupervised training increased and he consistently attended supervised sessions, with no qualifying AECOPD. Phase 2 6MWD rose 244→276 m, CAT 23→16, SGRQ symptoms 77→67 and CSQ-8 21→26 from Phase 2 baseline to week 8. Other SGRQ domains did not uniformly improve: total 55→56, impact 34→39 and activity unchanged at 80. No adverse events/dropouts were reported, but formal adherence/usability were not assessed and anxiety/depression were not fully evaluated. Follow-up was limited to the intervention; causal prevention or longer-term benefit is not established.

Authors judge that the observed 6MWD and CAT changes exceeded published minimal clinically important differences, and the abstract reports improved adherence although formal adherence assessment was not conducted.
